                    Public Utility Commission of Texas

                                     Memorandum


 TO:            Chairman Thomas J. Gleeson
                Commissioner Kathleen Jackson
                Commissioner Courtney Hjaltman
                Commissioner Morgan Johnson
                Commissioner Patrick Rhode

 FROM:          Barksdale English, Deputy Executive Director
                Harika Basaran, Division Director, Market Analysis
                Jessie Horn, Sr. Counsel, Rules and Projects Division

 DATE:          April 12, 2026

 RE:            April 17, 2026 Open Meeting Agenda Item No. 23
                Project No. 59142, Review of ERCOT’s Interconnection Processes for Large
                Loads


Over the last eighteen months, Texas has seen unprecedented growth in the number of large
load customers—data center and crypto-mining facilities, in particular—seeking to
interconnect in the ERCOT region. To more efficiently process the large volume of
interconnection requests that it must study to preserve reliable grid operations, ERCOT has
committed to implementing a process in which it studies large load customers’ requests for
interconnection in batches.

Batch Zero is the transitional step towards implementation of this new process and is necessary
to clear the backlog of interconnection requests that ERCOT has received from large load
customers choosing to bring their business to Texas for its abundance in natural resources and
unparalleled speed to interconnect. Recently, ERCOT reported that the large load
interconnection request queue has reached 400 gigawatts (GW), which is five times ERCOT’s
current peak load of 85 GW. ERCOT’s 2025 Regional Transmission Plan forecast that
approximately 85 GW of large loads would interconnect by 2031, revealing a massive
disconnect between what customers claim and what transmission planners believe to be
realistic requests for interconnection. Some refer to these speculative requests as ‘phantom
load’ and they represent a significant planning challenge for ERCOT and the transmission
utilities operating in the region.

Selecting the Batch Zero criteria—both technical and financial—ERCOT will use to determine
which of the large load projects in the queue are base load and which projects are studied load
are pivotal decisions. Base loads should be comprised of those large load customers that have
an interconnection study that ERCOT deems valid. This is necessary to ensure Batch Zero does
not exceed transmission system reliability limits mandated by the North American Electric
Reliability Corporation. Large load customers in this category have already received an

                                            Page 1 of 4
 Project No. 59142                    Staff Recommendations for Batch Zero


allocation of transmission capacity to serve their load and do not need to be restudied in Batch
Zero. Inclusion as a base load in Batch Zero must provide certainty to large load developers
that their projects will be able to interconnect on the timeline prescribed in earlier planning
studies.

Studied loads, on the other hand, should be comprised of those large load projects that do not
have an interconnection study that ERCOT deems valid 1 and therefore need to be restudied in
Batch Zero to determine to what extent and by when ERCOT can reliably serve the large load
customer’s requested capacity. These studied loads may receive an allocation of transmission
capacity that is initially less than their requested amount. While there is general consensus
among the stakeholder community, ERCOT Staff, and Commission Staff that Batch Zero must
aim to filter the queue of phantom loads and protect ratepayers in a manner that supports
business development and to ensure reliability of the ERCOT grid, there is disagreement about
how best to achieve those objectives.

On March 4, 2026, ERCOT introduced Planning Guide Revision Request (PGRR) 145 to
establish the process and procedures for Batch Zero, as well as the entry criteria for determining
base load and studied load. PGRR 145 is currently working its way through the ERCOT
stakeholder process and will be presented to the ERCOT Board of Directors in its final form
in June. Following approval by the ERCOT Board of Directors, the Commission will consider
PGRR 145 during a subsequent open meeting.

Because of the importance of PGRR 145 and its timely implementation, Commission Staff
requests guidance from the Commission at the April 17, 2026 open meeting to help inform the
appropriate criteria that stakeholders and ERCOT should consider including as they work
towards refining PGRR 145.

To facilitate the Commission’s discussion of this important matter at the open meeting,
Commission Staff has attached to this memorandum a table of proposed criteria, some of which
overlap with the current draft of PGRR 145 and some of which represent a departure from the
current draft of PGRR 145.

In addition to the criteria detailed in the attached table, Commission Staff recommends
consideration of these other important concepts:
    •    Non-Refundability of Financial Commitments: PGRR 145 should not include details
         about whether or what portion of a financial commitment is refundable because these
         parameters are beyond ERCOT’s authority. The refundability provisions in proposed
         16 TAC § 25.194 should clearly associate financial security with various stages in the
         project development timeline, ensure that utilities can draw against security for certain
         development milestones, and provide for an escalating amount of non-refundable
         security tied to those milestones.


         1
            Validation may require completion of a restudy to consider the impact of other new large load
customers added in the same area since the initial study was conducted and verifies that the large load customer
can still be served reliably.



                                                Page 2 of 4
 Project No. 59142              Staff Recommendations for Batch Zero


    •   Application of Withheld Financial Commitment: ERCOT’s rules should not address
        how any withheld portion of a financial commitment is applied. The final draft of 16
        TAC § 25.194 should reflect that any withheld portion of financial commitment should
        be applied to reducing a utility’s annual revenue requirement rather than reducing a
        utility’s rate base.
    •   Controllable Load Resources: ERCOT and stakeholders should continue developing
        parameters that would allow inclusion of some CLRs in Batch Zero.
    •   Minimum Capacity Allocation: ERCOT should establish a 100 MW transmission
        capacity allocation minimum to ensure meaningful outcomes for Batch Zero projects.
